The vault on the other side.

A closer look at the mechanics described in the FloatSheets product overview and backend specification.

IN THIS NOTEPool versus trader.Spread and funding respond to risk.Liquidity opens with a track record.A dedicated layer absorbs gap losses.Explore safely with virtual balances.Explore dashboard ↗
{01}

Pool versus trader.

The planned engine uses a liquidity vault as the counterparty to trader positions. Execution is based on the oracle price plus or minus a dynamic spread. It does not use an order book or an AMM price curve.

{02}

Spread and funding respond to risk.

The spread reflects price confidence and directional skew. Funding responds to the imbalance between long and short open interest. Position profit and loss settles in USDG.

{03}

Liquidity opens with a track record.

The product roadmap gates outside LP deposits until the engine has live operating history. LP participation appears in F3 alongside advanced order types and an API. No yield or return is promised by this frontend.

{04}

A dedicated layer absorbs gap losses.

Junior insurance capital supports the loss-absorbing tranche. After the insurance fund, this tranche can absorb gap losses before LP principal. Capital providers must understand that this layer is exposed to loss.

{05}

Explore safely with virtual balances.

The workspace vault moves virtual USDG between your local account and a simulated vault balance. There are no token approvals, deposits, withdrawals, or blockchain transactions.
